sections.title: Red Flags: When to Suspect LHON
content: Painless, subacute sequential vision loss in one eye followed by the other within weeks/months.
Profound dyschromatopsia (red-green deficiency) out of proportion to acuity.
Absence of pain on eye movement (differentiates from Optic Neuritis).
Family history of sudden blindness in maternal relatives.
Young male presenting with cecocentral scotoma.

rows: Optic nerve head pallor, RNF loss

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol
content: Step 1: Careful history (maternal lineage) and clinical exam.
Step 2: Fundoscopy (look for characteristic telangiectatic microangiopathy).
Step 3: OCT (RNFL thickness analysis - note initial swelling followed by thinning).
Step 4: Visual Field (Humphrey 30-2: typically dense cecocentral scotoma).
Step 5: Genetic testing (Mitochondrial DNA blood panel for the 3 primary mutations).

sections.title: Management & Therapeutic Advances
content: Idebenone (Short-chain Coenzyme Q10 analogue): Improves mitochondrial ATP production. Approved at 900mg/day (divided dose).
Gene Therapy: Lumevoq (Lenadogene nolparvovec) - viral vector delivery of wild-type ND4 gene via intravitreal injection.
Avoidance of toxic factors: Strict cessation of tobacco and ethanol consumption.
Neuro-ophthalmological monitoring: Frequent follow-up for the fellow eye.

content.explanation: L: Loss (Subacute), H: Hereditary (Maternal), O: Optic Nerve (Pseudo-edema), N: ND4/ND1/ND6 mutations.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Pseudo-disc edema does not leak on Fluorescein Angiography.
The '14484' mutation has a significantly better prognosis for spontaneous visual recovery.
Mitochondrial genes are not affected by Mendelian inheritance laws (maternal only).
LHON-Plus syndrome: consider if patient exhibits dystonia, tremor, or cardiac conduction defects.

sections.title: --- Sub-topics from: LHON: The Mitochondrial Silent Thief of Sight ---
sections.content: Leber Hereditary Optic Neuropathy (LHON) is the most common primary mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) disorder, characterized by subacute, painless, bilateral central vision loss primarily affecting young males. It represents a paradigm of mitochondrial genetics and selective retinal ganglion cell (RGC) vulnerability.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: LHON is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disease resulting from mutations in the ND genes (encoding subunits of Complex I of the respiratory chain). It causes selective apoptosis of Retinal Ganglion Cells (RGCs), specifically the parvocellular pathway, leading to severe optic atrophy and permanent central scotoma.

sections.title: Clinical Progression Stages
content: Step 1: Asymptomatic Carrier (Normal acuity, subclinical RNFL thickening)
Step 2: Subacute Phase (Weeks 0-6): Rapid painless vision loss, dyschromatopsia
Step 3: Dynamic Phase (Months 1-6): Fellow eye involved (sequential > simultaneous)
Step 4: Chronic Phase (>6-12 Months): Progressive RNFL loss, optic atrophy

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Peripapillary telangiectatic microangiopathy
Pseudo-edema: Swelling of the nerve fiber layer (NFL) without leakage
Absence of Optic Disc Cupping (unlike glaucoma)
Tortuosity of retinal arterioles
Centrocecal scotoma on Visual Field testing
Pupillary light reflex is often DISPROPORTIONATELY spared

sections.title: Diagnostic Investigation Workup
content: Genetic Testing: Targeted screening for the 3 primary mutations
OCT RNFL/GCL: Shows temporal thinning followed by global atrophy
Fluorescein Angiography (FFA): CRITICAL to show NO disc leakage
Visual Field (Goldmann or HVF): Demonstrates central/centrocecal scotomas
Neuroimaging (MRI): To rule out compressive or demyelinating lesions

sections.title: Red Flags & Contraindications
content: Smoking: Strongest environmental trigger for conversion
Excessive Alcohol: Synergistic effect with tobacco
Ethambutol/Linezolid: Avoid mitochondrial toxins
Rapid, Painful loss: Consider inflammatory etiology instead
Extraocular Signs: 'LHON Plus' (Dystonia, tremors, MS-like symptoms)

content.explanation: S: SYMMETRIC (eventually), S: SUBACUTE (painless), S: SMOKING (must stop!)

sections.title: Management & Treatment Protocol
content: Step 1: Lifestyle Modification: Immediate cessation of smoking and limited alcohol consumption.
Step 2: Idebenone (Raxone): 900mg/day (300mg TID). Start early for best results, continue for at least 1 year.
Step 3: Gene Therapy (Lumevoq/GS010): Intravitreal injection of rAAV2/2-ND4. Recent studies show bilateral benefit after unilateral injection.
Step 4: Supportive Care: Low vision aids and genetic counseling for maternal relatives.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: LHON is often misdiagnosed as 'Retrobulbar Optic Neuritis' in the early phase.
Fenestration of the optic nerve sheath is CONTRAINDICATED.
The pseudo-edema corresponds to stasis of axoplasmic transport, NOT fluid.
Melanopsin-containing RGCs are spared, explaining the preserved pupillary reflex.
Wait at least 12-18 months before declaring no chance of spontaneous recovery.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: RESCUE & REVERSE Trials: Evaluated Lumevoq gene therapy for ND4 mutations.
REFLECT Trial: Confirmed the efficacy of bilateral IVT gene therapy injections.
RHODOS Trial: Provided the evidence base for high-dose Idebenone (900mg/day).
The 'Bilateral Benefit' Phenomenon: Discovery of viral vector transfer via the optic chiasm.
